Daylight saving time: Why many Americans are riled - BBC News

Well we went through the spring time ritual of setting our clocks forward again. But our biological clocks are not reset as easily. One only needs to look back at the original reason for DST to determine if it is still useful. It was instituted when America was an agrarian country and farmers used the extra daytime hour for tending the fields. Of course they had no artificial lights then. So like many government instituted things they persist long after their usefulness expires.

Farmers operated by sunlight, not by clocks. Changing the dial on the clock didn't make sunup come any sooner, or sunset happen any later.

It was more about people not turning on artificial lighting in the evening, which we don't really care that much about anymore, especially since most places are lit well beyond the extra hour anyway.
I can't express in words how pleased I would be if we finally did away with this bullshit.
Well, I enjoy seeing people running late and cackling at them. But I'm not exactly normal, so...
It's pretty much no longer a hassle as everyone has a cell phone that automatically sets the time. So there is no disruption and forgetting to set the clocks. But it's still stupid.

I did not grow up with DST. Nor does it exist in tropical countries. I make good use of it, though: people who like DST, people who defend DST, people who tell me stories about "farmers" -- I know they are idiots. Could an absolutely idiotic bill of no use to anyone pass through our legislative bodies? It already has -- DST. Could a society participate in a mass delusion whereby they think they dictate nature? I don't need to hear about FaceBook's 51 genders. I don't need to think back to King Canute. I get reminded of Collective Delusion Time twice a year.

Humans are dumb. They have been for a long time.
